name: PWX Championship
epitaph: The fed's own title history lists 19 reigns of the PWX Championship, from Michael Norcia on 30 September 2005 to Brian Hollywood's second, read as 25 January 2010. The title was vacated when PWX announced its closure in December 2007 and was next decided on 18 October 2009, at Never Say Die 2009, when Ness won it from Jackson.
notes: The page calls it the one title every wrestler strives for, PWX's equivalent of a world title though PWX does not recognize it as a world championship.

name: PWX Hybrid Championship
epitaph: The fed's own title history lists 24 reigns of the Hybrid Championship, from John Pariah on 2 September 2005 to Terrell Odom, who won it on 7 December 2009 and was stripped of it for injury on 18 January 2010. The page says it can be contested under any rules and by wrestlers of any style.
notes: The page calls it the fed's most unique title: contested under any rules and fought for by wrestlers of any style, hence "Hybrid" wrestling.

name: PWX Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's own title history lists 21 numbered reigns of its tag titles, from Shocker and Mark O'Neal on 16 December 2005 to Corey Gein and Micheal Norcia on 28 October 2007, with the numbers 16 and 18 missing from the page. The last row records the titles vacated when PWX announced its closure in December 2007.
notes: The page says only the top tag teams in the world compete for these titles. Its heading reads "Campeones de Parejas".
